It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and no prima-facie case is made out against the applicants.
The applicant no.1 is husband and applicant no.2 is brother-in-law of informant.
Learned counsel has referred first information report as well as statement of informant and submitted that there are material contradictions in the version of informant.
In the first information report, she has stated that she has told her mother about the alleged incident of rape but in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has not stated any such fact.
The allegations of rape levelled against applicant no.2, are wholly false and improbable.
The version of informant is not supported by medical evidence.
In respect of co-accused persons, this Court has already granted interim relief.
Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that no case is made out against the applicants.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the application and submitted that applicant no.1 is husband of informant and there are several allegations against him.
Similarly, the informant has alleged that applicant no.2 has committed rape upon her.
It was submitted that in view of allegations made in the first information report and material collected during investigation, a prima-facie case is made out against the applicants.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. The legal position on the issue of quashing of criminal proceedings is well-settled that the jurisdiction to quash a complaint, FIR or a charge-sheet should be exercised sparingly and only in exceptional cases.

However, where the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and material on record even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused, the charge-sheet may be quashed in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.

In well celebrated judgement reported in AIR 1992 SC 605 State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajan Lal, Supreme Court has carved out certain guidelines, wherein FIR or proceedings may be quashed but cautioned that the power to quash FIR or proceedings should be exercised sparingly and that too in the rarest of rare cases.

sentences.text: It has been held that if a prima facie case is made out disclosing ingredients of the offence, court should not quash the charge sheet/complaint.
It is equally well settled that at this stage questions of fact cannot be examined and a mini trial cannot be held.
7. In the instant matter, perusal of record shows that marriage of informant with applicant no.1 has taken place only a few months prior to the incident.
The informant has made clear allegations that she was harassed by the applicants and co-accused persons on account of dowry and they used to demand Rs.5 lakhs and a car as additional dowry.
She has also alleged that applicant no.2 has committed rape upon her.
The submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicants call for determination on questions of fact, which may adequately be discerned/adjudicated only by the trial court.
Even the submissions made on point of law can also be more appropriately gone into by the trial court.

In the instant matter, in view of allegations made in the first information report and the material collected during investigation, it cannot be said that no prima-facie case is made out Hasim And Another vs State Of U.P.
